name: He Who Fights With Monsters | Compendium Lorebook (spoiler level 0)
description: Derived from the HWFWM compendium (not a source). Spoiler level 0: public setting only. Book text takes precedence over the fan wiki; this file is regenerated by src/tools/lorebook.py.

key: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.comment: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.content: This primer is the foundation of the compendium. It explains the setting in plain language and summarises the facts that come up again and again. Later documents expand every section. Where a fact only becomes true later in the story it is marked (Later: Book N). The series follows Jason Asano, an ordinary Australian who is pulled out of his world by an accident and arrives, hairless and alone, in Pallimustus: a world very like Earth in size and shape, but soaked in magic. There, people absorb essences (crystallised magic), which give them supernatural abilities, and grow through ranks by hunting monsters and training. Adventurers, guilds, gods and rulers all depend on this system. Pallimustus has a twin, Earth, which was made from the same template but has much less magic, so its people do not know magic exists (at first). The two worlds are linked, and the link matters more and more as the story proceeds. In a roleplay you can set a story anywhere from the beginning (a rural iron-rank adventurer in Greenstone) to the end (a gold-rank world-defender at the edge of a cosmic war). Jason's powers revolve around afflictions (long-lasting debilitating effects). Many characters' signature lines are used as incantations ("Feed me your sins", "Mine is the judgement, and the judgement is death"). Team Biscuit: a familiar picked the team's name; Jason's biscuits are a running joke. Cloud houses are a signature aesthetic; so are floral shirts, board games and pop-culture references.
keys: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*
1.name: World Primer: the Worlds of *He Who Fights With Monsters*

2.content: Gods are transcendent beings outside physical reality, each focused on a single concept (Dominion, Healer, Knowledge, Death and more). They manifest avatars, speak with Akashic Speech, give followers essences and awakening stones that they can take back, and work miracles. Churches are their institutions.
2.name: Gods and Churches

3.content: An essence ability is a power an essence user has from an essence. Each essence gives five; one is awakened at absorption and the rest are awakened later by stones. Each ability has a type, a cost, a cooldown and a rank, and gains a new effect at each rank. Four attributes, Power, Speed, Spirit and Recovery, each bond to one of the four essences and rise in rank as that essence's abilities are mastered. Abilities and attributes together decide when a person can move up a rank. Special attack (melee, drain, wounding, blood): Leech Bite. Spell (drain): Blood Harvest. Special ability (dimension, teleport): Path of Shadows. Aura (holy, unholy): Hegemony. Conjuration (darkness, light, dimension): Cloak of Night. Familiar (ritual, summon): Sanguine Horror.
3.name: Abilities and Attributes

4.content: Adventuring is the work of killing monsters and clearing hazards for pay. In practice an adventurer is a licensed contractor: they take posted notices and contracts from a jobs hall, work in a team, and are paid in spirit coins and loot. Most are not heroes in the story sense, and the profession is as much about judgement and bookkeeping as combat. This file describes how the work runs. The organisation is described in 05_Organisations/Adventure_Society.md.
4.name: The Adventuring Profession

5.content: An affliction is a condition that harms its target for a time; a boon is a condition that helps. Both are named in brackets in System messages, carry tags (poison, disease, curse, holy, unholy, magic and others) and can stack. Defence against afflictions is a game of resisting, cleansing and negating: a cleanse removes an affliction, resistance reduces the chance or strength of one landing, and some afflictions are built to defeat both. In this world a character who understands which tool beats which condition has a large tactical advantage, and Jason's power set is built around that interplay.
5.name: Afflictions, Boons and Damage

6.content: Alongside essences and stones the world has a layer of working magic that does not need an essence: quintessence gems, spirit coins, potions, ointments, enchanted tools and growth items that rise in rank. This file describes what these materials are and how they are used. It does not list individual named items; those are in 09_Items_and_Artefacts/.
6.name: Alchemy, Artifice and Magical Materials

key: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
7.comment: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
7.content: Three kinds of event reshape territory in the series. Astral spaces are pocket worlds attached to a physical world through apertures. Proto-astral spaces are short-lived, unstable versions of them that Earth suffers from. Monster surges are periodic increases in monster numbers across a world. All four are driven by the same source: raw magic leaking through from the astral.
keys: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges
7.name: Astral Spaces, Transformation Zones and Surges

8.content: An aura is the projection of a ranked person's soul. It grows with rank, is read by other ranked people as a sense of danger, strength and mood, and is how adventurers judge each other before words are spoken. Controlling the aura is a skill with three basic parts: projecting it, restraining it and suppressing other people's. Auras can be hidden, masked, aimed at normal people to intimidate them, and, at silver rank, begin to lift the body off the ground.
8.name: Auras

9.content: An awakening stone is a consumable crystal that awakens one essence ability the user has not yet awakened. It is the third kind of non-living magic Rufus lists, after essences and quintessence. The stone does not choose the ability; it steers toward a theme, and what comes out depends mostly on the essences the user holds. Stones are how a new essence user fills out the twenty abilities that a full set carries, and they are bought, auctioned, given as rewards and kept as family wealth.
9.name: Awakening Stones

10.content: A confluence is the fourth essence a person receives. It is not picked, bought or found. It is produced by the three essences already absorbed, and it arrives the moment the third is used. In the main run of the series a given trio of essences always gives the same confluence, and the Magic Society keeps a list of the known trios. Confluences are rated and talked about as if they were essences in their own right, and many of the best-known power sets belong to a confluence.
10.name: Confluences

11.content: The books name far more essences than the wiki lists give with evidence. This file collects those the text actually shows, with who holds them and what the text says of their behaviour. Rarity statements come from the text; where the text gives none, none is invented. It is intended as a quick reference for building a character's power set, not as a mechanical list. The full set of essences the Magic Society knows is in its living document. The wiki's fuller lists of essences, confluences and combinations are in../Appendices/Wiki_Reference_Lists.md, with a cross-reference to the first book line for each entry found in the text. Where the wiki gives a rarity, it agrees with the text so far: sin is Legendary, renewal is Epic and rune and vast are among the highest.
11.name: Essence Catalogue

12.content: An essence is the most powerful and rarest of the forms in which magic condenses into something that is not alive. It is absorbed into a person's soul and gives that person a set of five abilities tied to its concept. Four essences make a full set. A person with a full set becomes iron rank and is changed by it. Essences are how Pallimustus makes essence users: the people who fight monsters, serve in the churches and run most of the world's institutions.
12.name: Essences

13.content: A familiar is a creature made or called to serve one person for life. A summoned familiar is built by ritual from magical materials and a being drawn from the deep astral; a bonded familiar is a creature that answers a call. Familiars are different from the short-lived summons many essence users can conjure in the middle of a fight, and from conjurations, which are things drawn out of mana. All three are essence abilities and come from awakening stones or from the essences themselves; none can be used by anyone who lacks the necessary ritual knowledge.
13.name: Familiars, Summons and Conjurations

14.content: An essence user can grow in power in two ways. One is to consume monster cores, which is easy and can be bought. The other is to train, fight real danger and meditate. Rufus's teaching in Book 1 is that the first method eats into the potential of the second. The setting's politics, from the aristocratic families of Greenstone to the Network on Earth, turn on which method a group has used, and on what it costs them later.
14.name: Monster Cores and Training

15.content: Monsters are the most common way magic manifests in a magic-rich world. They appear from nothing, usually in the wild, live for a time that depends on their rank, and then dissolve back into raw magic if not killed first. They have ranks like essence users; the ranks are not given by essences but by the density of the magic that makes them. Hunting them before they reach their aggressive final stage is the bulk of an adventurer's work, and what they leave behind funds much of the economy.
15.name: Monsters

16.content: Rank is the world's measure of power. It runs from normal people through iron, bronze, silver, gold and diamond; beyond diamond are gods and great astral beings, who are not part of the ladder. Essence users and monsters share the ladder, and each rank "has a suppressive effect on lower ranks". Rank changes the body, the length of life, what a person can do with their aura and the way other people treat them. It is the setting's class system.
16.name: Ranks and Advancement

17.content: Ritual magic is the practice of drawing a diagram, a circle with lines and glyphs, and powering it with external magic to do something an essence ability cannot. It is used for absorbing essences, awakening stones, summoning familiars, spreading wards and tracking, and, in permanent form, as formations and arrays. Ritual magic is learned, not given by an essence, and a competent ritualist is a valuable member of any team. Anyone can learn external magic; only essence users can combine it with essence powers.
17.name: Rituals, Arrays and Formations

18.content: A skill book is a consumable magical book that implants knowledge directly into the reader. It can teach a language, a martial art, the basics of ritual magic or a branch of astral magic. A skill book gives technique and information, not understanding or practice, and the people who use them well prepare beforehand and consolidate afterwards. They are the fast, flawed route to ability in a skill, in the same way that cores are the fast, flawed route to rank.
18.name: Skill Books and Learning

19.content: A soul is the part of a person that essences and ranks change. It shapes the body, projects the aura, leaves marks when wounded and, on death, lingers briefly before drifting into the astral. Healing magic can reverse a death only in that grace period and only with powerful magic. Everyday healing is done by the Healer's church, by alchemists and by healing abilities, and it is in short supply compared to demand.
19.name: Souls, Death and Healing

20.content: Most magic in the setting follows the essence-and-rank structure described elsewhere in this folder. A smaller body of magic does not: the gifts a person is born with or earns as a race, the outworlder abilities that give Jason a game-like interface, titles drawn from soul damage, time magic, and the powers of great astral beings and gods. This file collects them so a storyteller knows what exists and who has what. It does not attempt to explain the cosmology; see 02_Cosmology_and_Powers/. Interface: the screens and System messages; "interpret reality through a recognisable medium". Quest System: quests with rewards, including a "racial gift transfiguration". Inventory: a grid of forty slots with a currency counter; items are plucked from and pushed into the screen. Astral Affinity: "Increased resistance to dimension effects and astral forces. Dimension abilities have increased effect and transcendent damage is increased". Mysterious Stranger: "Language adaptation. Essence, awakening stone and skill-book absorption. Immunity to identification and tracking effects".
20.name: Unusual and Unique Magic

21.content: Metallic-haired, metallic-eyed people with an astral affinity, produced when two outworlders have a child. Appearance: Sophie has chocolate skin and shining silver hair, her eyes matching it exactly, "the matching metallics a giveaway trait of the celestine race". In Kurdansk many celestines have dark skin and silver hair. Astral affinity: astral affinity is a celestine racial gift; celestines are similar to elves and humans. The rare Child of the Celestial Wind appears only in races with astral affinity, on Pallimustus meaning celestines, or potentially outworlders. Origin: Dawn says two outworlders who have a child produce a celestine, and celestines propagate with their own kind; she is herself a child of two outworlders. Gift evolutions: Sophie's Mana Integrity becomes Mana Wellspring, her Astral Affinity becomes Boundary Breaker and her Celestial Swiftness becomes Princess of the Firmament. Communities: Zartos is a subterranean city largely populated by celestines. Messengers: messengers are about half again as tall as a celestine, and their servants take care never to imply the resemblance. Dawn's true form: a celestine with ruby eyes and hair.
21.name: Celestines

key: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
22.comment: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
22.content: The practical texture of life in Greenstone and the delta: the calendar, what people wear and eat, how they travel and what runs on spirit coins. Calendar: "twelve months of thirty days, divided up into early, mid and late stages of each season", five extra days for the solstices, equinoxes and the new year, which falls at the beginning of spring. The week has six days. Clothing: "Most people, whether in Greenstone or the delta, wore loose-fitting, breathable clothes because of the heat"; adventurers on a job wear fitted outfits, often with protective properties. Elf fashion has flowing, tapered lines. Food: preparation is often familiar, with bread, soup, sandwiches and cake, but the ingredients are mostly different because farms raise different animals and trees bear different fruit. Jason lists local sauce ingredients with a village cook. Housing: Leust, one of the delta's largest towns, has paved roads and stone buildings "instead of mud-brick"; in the Island, green stone appears everywhere. Transport: heidels are "the size and shape of a horse, but with scales instead of hair and two heads, each with a horn"; the Island's districts are linked by a subterranean, submarine transit line called the loop, with terminals laid out like train stations. Devices: lamps, showers and most household magic run on lesser spirit coins.
keys: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport
22.name: Daily Life: Calendar, Food, Clothing and Transport

23.content: Large, scaled humanoids who claim descent from dragons and whose homeland is the Dragon Lands. Appearance: "a member of the rare draconian race, larger even than male leonids and covered in glossy scales", the colour of dark leaves, green moving into purple; Maximilian is the tallest person in Greenstone, with a long hairless head and glossy scales. A draconian skull is distinctive enough to identify skeletons. Pride in descent: draconians "took pride in their claimed dragon ancestry and often had issues with other races wielding the dragon essence". Homeland: the Dragon Lands, Pallimustus's version of Antarctica, "the native land of the large, scaled humanoids known as draconians", with active volcanoes, hot springs and "dragon mouth" geysers from subterranean apertures to a realm of fire. Rarity: draconians are rare in Greenstone, where Maximilian is the only one present at a gathering.
23.name: Draconians

24.content: How money works on Pallimustus: spirit coins in six denominations that also power devices and sustain essence users, farms that make them, and who controls them. Denominations: "The basic coin of the realm was the lesser spirit coin. Iron spirit coins were worth a hundred lesser coins, used by bulk traders, adventurers and other members of the wealthy elite. After that, it was ten iron to the bronze, ten bronze to the silver and ten silver to the gold"; three gold coins are "worth three hundred thousand units of the basic currency". Why the lesser coin is the basic unit: higher-rank coins are "not very useful for everyday life"; almost all home and business magic devices, such as lamps and showers, run on lesser coins and higher ranks would burn them out, while larger infrastructure such as the loop line uses more powerful coins. Sustenance: ranked people can live on spirit coins; Rufus says a bronze coin will sustain bronze-rank adventurers without stressing their bodies, so it is about not going over your limit. Farms: spirit coins are made on farms using special moulds that cause magic to crystallise, in delicate, very stable ambient magic.
24.name: Economy and Money

25.content: Elves are powerful spellcasters whose healing magic is unparalleled. Reputation: "Elves are powerful spell casters and their skill with healing magic is unparalleled". Aptitude: the elven aptitude is for spells rather than the special attacks humans favour. Racial gift: Neil's elf racial ability, Life Affinity, evolves into Life Guard. Local families: Greenstone has local elf families; Lucian Lamprey is an elf banished there who is not one of them, and Pochard Finn is an elf and a local. Elf fashion: "flowing, tapered lines". Notable elves: Allayeth and Charist, Yaresh's two diamond-rank elves; Hana Shavar, High Priestess of the Healer; Elspeth Arella, director of the Greenstone Adventure Society. Predation: cannibals in Book 1 discuss elves as food.
25.name: Elves

key: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
26.comment: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
26.content: A large, densely populated kingdom of old noble houses, garden towers and high-magic farmland, and the homeland from which Greenstone was colonised. Standing: "One of the most prominent kingdoms in the world" with a royal family; the Queen of Estercost and other members of its elite ask Jason to arbitrate over the System's withdrawal. Population: a "large and densely populated kingdom" and the land from which Greenstone was colonised centuries earlier; the region is "filled with towns, villages and smaller cities, due to the idyllic climate and rich natural resources". Vitesse: the city of flowers, on what Jason would know as the French Riviera, with garden towers that house the wealthy elite and key organisations. Adventurers think of it as the continent's adventuring capital, because its high magic spawns powerful, frequent monster manifestations. Aristocracy: the Remore family has no title, while the Gellers hold only the title from their small provincial city of origin and refuse all others; neither is begrudged a premier tower. Cyrion's laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families". House Headingway is "one of Estercost's pre-eminent families". Cyrion's land: concentric walls ring the city with vast tracts of agricultural land between them, "some of the most magical and valuable growing land on the planet"; it is the largest city in the world, with lakes, forests and heavy air traffic.
keys: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats
26.name: Estercost: Culture of a Kingdom of Aristocrats

27.content: Goblins and fairies appear as monsters and as people of Earth transformed by the zones; fairies are also a small hovering manifestation. Goblins as monsters: Jason jokes about killing ten goblins for an uncommon spear in the cannibals' cave. Transformed humans: in West Canfield, Detroit, people were "turned into goblins and their homes into underground warrens", which became a lawless combat zone. Cabal beings: the Cabal's mythological beings include centaurs, ogres, fairies and more. Elves, goblins and fairies: people in a magic city were "turned into elves and goblins and fairies". Fairy manifestation: a small hovering fairy-like figure with an androgynous body bites Clive in Book 2.
27.name: Goblins and Fairies: Zone-Transformed Peoples

28.content: The most common people of Pallimustus and Earth's native people, with gifts that favour special attacks and fast essence advancement. Racial gifts: an affinity for special attacks, essences that advance more rapidly than others', and latent powers that adapt to the essences. The latent gifts are dormant until awakened and then take a form based on the person's essences. Evolution: Clive's blessing from the Celestial Book changes his human special attack affinity into a spell affinity; his Human Ambition becomes Thirst for Knowledge and Humphrey's Special Attack Affinity becomes Attack of the Mirage Dragon. Taika's human abilities have been replaced with outworlder ones. Distribution: the Greenstone region is human-dominated. Humans and outworlders: an outworlder who has a child with another species produces offspring of that species, so a human and an outworlder have a human child. Lifespan: essence users age slower; bronze-rankers can live well past a hundred, silvers double that and gold-rankers live for centuries.
28.name: Humans

key: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
29.comment: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
29.content: A river city in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil, where celestines with dark skin and silver hair are common, entertainment and crime share the old docks, and prisons rather than indenture punish crime. Nation: Kurdansk lies "in the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil". Celestines: "Like many of Kurdansk's celestines, she had dark skin and silver hair", and the rowhouses are narrow and wedged together. Entertainment quarter: a former warehouse district near the Kurdan River docks, now the most viable site for large theatre halls, "a heady mix of pleasure, criminality and money". Skyport: it has a busy skyport with towers where airships dock.
keys: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil
29.name: Kurdansk: Culture of the People's Holy Federation of Dreisil

30.content: ; Indenture, not slavery: "We don't have slaves. We have indentured servants. A lot of criminals are sentenced to indenture, then their indenture is sold or auctioned to recoup the cost of their crimes". Jason finds the system disturbing and says both his world and this one need better systems. Captured enemies: the Ustei do not accept slavery; "their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death". The Adventure Society agreement: a clause in the Adventure Society's agreement with Greenstone gives anyone who completes a contract the right of refusal on anyone sentenced to indenture as a result of it. Hearings: indenture hearings are a normal legal event; the Greenstone court "was less like an American legal p[roceeding]". House guards: in Cyrion, house guards are "technically a form of indentured servitude" and the laws "were very much built to favour the aristocratic families". Jason's argument: if a family used "draconian measures" to hold people to cheap work, nothing would stop them. The System's withdrawal: the System will withdraw access "in regions of Pallimustus currently operating with slavery, indentured servitude or similar legal systems". "The Queen of Estercost and several other interested parties" ask for arbitration over the withdrawal. Slave markets: Jason's friend scouts Sadi Andali's slave markets, and Ben asks whether "the destruction of the Sadi Andali slave trade" is Jason's price.
30.name: Law and Indenture

31.content: Lion-headed, furred, strong and fast people; Gary is the best-known leonid. Strength and stamina: "Members of his leonid race are stronger and faster than us, and that's only the beginning of what leonids can do"; a leonid needs far more exertion than others to tire, another racial gift. Appearance: a huge "lion man" whose voice is growly by default; Gary is "so huge he made bodybuilders look like they w[ere small]". He is covered in fur. Size: draconians are larger even than male leonids.
31.name: Leonids

32.content: Merfolk are named once in the books as people, not fish; no detail beyond that is established here. Only reference: Emir answers a joke about someone's partner ("Man, woman or fish?") with "Merfolk are not fish. They happen to be very sensual people". Open gap: no chapter text found so far gives merfolk appearance, homeland or gifts.
32.name: Merfolk

33.content: People whose souls re-entered a physical reality, manifesting a new body; they carry unusual gifts and cannot be easily tracked. Definition: Clive: "An outworlder is someone whose soul has re-entered a physical reality, reflexively manifesting a body for itself"; the body is "akin to that of a monster, or a summoned familiar", physical substance forged from raw magic, between the astral and the physical. How it happens: natural magical phenomena connecting two realities drag someone through; their body is annihilated in the astral and their soul reconstitutes one. Advantages: Farrah says outworlders "might have their advantages", and Jason's abilities (map, interface, astral affinity) are outworlder abilities. Children: an outworlder with another species produces offspring of that species; two outworlders produce a celestine.
33.name: Outworlders

key: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
34.comment: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
34.content: The large southern land corresponding to Sri Lanka, where portal stopovers and isolated city-states form a trading hub, and where Jayapura is the port Hester calls home. Geography: Pranay is this world's equivalent of Sri Lanka, "larger and further south", a huge landmass in the Indian Ocean. Its northern coast has several important sea-trade connections in a world without the Arabian Peninsula. Jayapura: Hester's birth city; personal transport for those who can afford it is a platter-sized floating disc ridden by shifting weight. Mirage chambers: Jayapura has a vast mirage chamber complex, more sophisticated than the Gellers' private chamber in Greenstone because the higher magic allows potent dimensional magic and concurrent chambers. Massive city: Jason's team visited Pranay's urban centre after their first Reaper astral space and saw only familiars as magical beasts.
keys: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States
34.name: Pranay: Culture of the Isolated City-States

35.content: How faith appears day to day: crowded temple districts with hierarchies of their own, churches that serve as hospitals and archives, and gods whose rules limit what they can do. Temple districts: temples line the road to the Island's Divine Square and "gods had hierarchies of their own": the Temple of Roads sits behind the larger Temple of Journeys. The square is crowded with booths selling religious paraphernalia and people proselytising. Dominion: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles. It is he who determines who rules, and who serves". The Healer: Neil makes a stand in the Temple of the Healer; ex-clergy who offended their gods and were stripped of divinely gifted essences suffer a debilitating imbalance in body and soul; the notes make the Healer the god who does this. Knowledge's temple: in Rimaros it is "an important resource for the many magical researchers" with a symbiotic relationship with the Magic Society branch; the temple is mostly a vast library covering multiple wings. Churches and research: churches, especially Knowledge's, help fund the Magical Research Association. Death's paperwork: the Church of Death issues certification of how many times a person has died. Limits on gods: a god's favour does not mean intervention; a goddess says she cannot see into the astral space where Jason holds prisoners; the gods are "bound by convoluted limitations".
35.name: Religion in Practice

36.content: Short, stocky, hairless people with deep-blue skin and naturally glowing runes. Appearance: "short and stocky, with skin of such a deep blue it was almost black", no hair and covered in faintly glowing, tattoo-like markings that are natural to the race. Rarity: they are "a rarity in Greenstone"; a runic barman in Old City is stocky and hairless with blue-black skin and glowing runes. Bones: the runes show faintly on their bones; a short, broad skeleton in the desert astral space is identified as a runic by them. Notable: Arash, a runic Jason meets in the temple district, explains Dominion's role: "Dominion issues the divine right to kings and nobles". Part of the civilisation-building species: the list of species that build civilisations is "humans, elves and leonids, celestines, runic, smoulder and draconians". Common in Old City: a runic works as a barman, and a runic man appears at Jory's clinic.
36.name: Runics

37.content: Dark-skinned people with glowing red eyes and affinities for earth and fire; the brighthearts are the smoulder of the deep underground realm of Cardinas. Smoulder: "They have natural affinities for earth and fire"; a smoulder friend of Humphrey's parents has the wind essence and his earth affinity evolved into an air affinity. Niko, a member of Beth's team, has dark skin, glowing red eyes and jet-black hair. Marla is a fire aspect with skin markings, eyes and hair the yellow-orange of steel in a forge; Lorenn, an ash aspect, has smoky greys. War form: Beaufort prefers his fifteen-foot metal skeleton "war form" but must meet the brightheart smoulders in a form they will accept. Home: the largest chamber of the underground realm was home to most brightheart smoulders.
37.name: Smoulder and Brighthearts

key: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
38.comment: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
38.content: A sea kingdom ruled from Rimaros, where a gold-rank monarch rules, heirs prove themselves as adventurers, and sky islands house the cream of society. Extent: "It rules the Sea of Storms, all the islands on it and all the coastal regions that surround it"; the capital is Rimaros. Sky islands: reserved for "the cream of society": big-name adventurers, long-standing adventuring families and aristocrats; a family known for producing good adventurers is mostly inducted into the nobility, and a house without good adventurers sinks into obscurity. Monarchy: the Storm King is a gold-ranker, which one must be to take the throne; royals are not raised on cores as in most nations, since that disqualifies them here, and potential heirs from every branch are adventurers proving themselves in monster fighting and statecraft in a decades-long contest until the monarch chooses an heir. Titles: the firstborn daughter of the Storm King, if competing, is the Hurricane Princess and the firstborn son the Storm Prince; many royals bow out, often adopting into their non-royal parent's family. Palindromic names: first and last names that are palindromes are assigned in adulthood and mark important family members; the more prominent the family, the rarer the practice, and the royal family shares a name with the capital. Royal looks: the royal family's iconic feature is sapphire hair and eyes.
keys: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms
38.name: The Storm Kingdom: Culture of Rimaros and the Sea of Storms

39.content: A nomad tribe from a region to the north that raids spirit coin convoys in the Greenstone desert and will not accept captured warriors as slaves. Who they are: the "sand pirates" are actually the Ustei Tribe, nomads from a region to the north; Humphrey identifies them as northerners from their hair and clothes. The raids: an expedition is formed to find out why they are so far south and stop them raiding spirit coin shipments. The response: the best outcome is a peaceful return north or an agreement not to attack convoys; failing that, they are to be captured and interrogated. Vincent expects them to talk if shown strength. Captives: "Their culture doesn't allow warriors to be made slaves. For them, capture means release or death".
39.name: The Ustei: Northern Nomad Tribe

key: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
40.comment: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
40.content: A small-population city that grows around its trees, whose civic government is weaker than its churches and societies, and whose two elf diamond-rankers dominate its adventuring scene. Size and design: only a few tens of thousands live there, but the design accommodates the environment so that the city has the footprint of a much larger centre. Walls and gates: its walls are a line of massive trees with glossy black stone filling the gaps, tunnels pass through the trunks, and vehicles queue at a gate for inspection. Streets: alleys are nicer than the norm and resemble gardens, with gravel paths through long grass. Government: "In Yaresh, the civic administration is considerably weaker than the churches and the major societies", because one group undermines the Duke for its own ends. The Aristocratic Faction: wealthy aristocrats and a few merchant barons who own most of the land and provide most of the jobs, and who use that power to shape their tenants' ideology. They have no adventurers or researchers behind them, just money and political influence. Diamond-rankers: Allayeth and Charist, both elves; Yaresh has "not just one but two resident diamond-rankers", with Charist the more social and Allayeth the more reclusive, who raised the all-woman team Moon's Edge, led by Miriam Vance.
keys: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City
40.name: Yaresh: Culture of the Tree City

41.content: The Adventure Society is one of the three great organisations of Pallimustus. Its main purpose is monster extermination: it posts notices, issues contracts, assesses and registers adventurers, and keeps records of their kills. Its insignia is a sword and rod crossed over a shield, stitched on its staff's clothing and embossed on its badges. Restricted essences: Rufus says Death is restricted by itself, and the Magic Society's living document shows one restricted combination, the Succubus essence, which takes two insanely rare essences. A corrupt essence is on the list: a Magic-Society-bound adventurer hands one looted from an elemental to the Adventure Society "since it was on the restricted list"; the Society offers good trades for restricted essences. The wiki's fuller list and its Sacrifice-confluence pit fighter were not found in the text. Neutrality: the Society is described as neutral in disputes between nations. Corruption and reform: Rufus says there "may be some level of corruption in this branch" in Book 1; a later corruption enquiry at the Greenstone branch led to blanket demotions of two- and three-star members, who were bumped back up afterwards.
41.name: The Adventure Society

42.content: A guild is an adventuring organisation that recruits, trains and backs its members and takes on a share of the Adventure Society's work. Guilds carry weight in the Society's surge quotas and in politics. Great families have their own guilds or schools; some local powers (the Aristocratic Faction) deliberately avoid personal power.
42.name: Guilds, Houses and Local Powers

key: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
43.comment: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
43.content: The Magic Society records and regulates magic: it keeps the register of essences and their combinations, oversees spirit coin farms, runs communication networks and hoards research. The Alchemy Association and the Artifice Association are the guilds of the potion-makers and of the item-makers. The living document: a marble-and-gold tablet, connected to a central record, that updates as the record changes and holds the full list of every essence and essence combination known to the Society. It is how Farrah and Rufus look up what a combination will produce. Water link: the Society's chambers allow conversation at a distance. See../03_Magic_and_Adventuring/Alchemy_Artifice_and_Magical_Materials.md (communication). Spirit coin farms: registered farms exist. The Adventure Society treats anything touching the farms as three-star work. Greenstone branch: directed by Lucian Lamprey, who uses the Fortress as his office; his deputy director Pochard Finn is an elf and a local who runs the city campus and is "the de facto director of Greenstone's Magic Society". Pochard is Clive's boss. I haven't been deputy director for several years".
keys: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA
43.name: The Magic Society, the Associations and the MRA

44.content: Greenstone is a colony city at the mouth of a river delta in the low-magic far south of the Africa-like continent. It is the first city Jason knows on Pallimustus and the setting of most of Books 1-3. It was founded because its conditions suit low-end spirit coin farms: stable low magic, in a place that is also livable and close to the desert. It is a place of green marble, walled harbours, crime lords with gentlemanly manners, and a Society full of ambitious, mid-ranked people who use monster cores rather than fight for their ranks. Colonial status: the city began as a colony from the wider kingdom. The Adventure Society is a major force, but the isolation makes the local branch dependent on local powers; Rufus's remark to the village mayor is that "compromises must be made."; The Adventure Society branch is directed by Elspeth Arella. Vincent Trenslow runs assessments and assigns contracts. The Magic Society branch is directed by Lucian Lamprey, a silver-ranker who watches Fortress fights from a viewing box. His deputy is Pochard Finn, whose son Cassowary serves as Lucian's dogsbody. The Big Three of the underworld: Clarissa Ventress (mansion in the canal district), Cole Silva (obsessed with Sophie) and Adris Dorgan. They keep the underworld running and avoid gang war because it draws the attention of the Island authorities.
44.name: Greenstone

45.content: Vitesse, in the kingdom of Estercost, is the City of Flowers, "located in what Jason Asano would know as the French Riviera". Its skyline is made of the garden towers: huge towers with flowering vines spilling down the exterior, "most had every third or fourth floor dedicated to gardens using water, light and plant magic", which are residences for the wealthy elite and headquarters of key organisations. It is a high-magic, wealthy city (the social programmes and labour laws described below are not confirmed in the lines read). It is the home of Remore Academy and of Burning Violet, and the place Rufus, Gary and Farrah come from. Governed within the kingdom of Estercost. Remore family influence is pervasive: Roland Remore, a diamond-ranker who took over Burning Violet long ago, is the Academy's arch-chancellor and Rufus's grandfather. Burning Violet is the Remore family's elite guild. Strong labour protections and social programmes mean an unusually large comfortable middle class.
45.name: Vitesse

46.content: A water-and-islands astral space reached from the desert by a submerged aperture. A large Greenstone expedition goes in at the climax of Book 1 to find what is disrupting it. They are ambushed by a construct army.
46.name: The Desert Astral Space (Book 1)

47.content: Boko is an old desert city of academics and artists to the north of Greenstone, with a native population, a Duke, an Adventure Society branch and a Magic Society presence. Jason first arrives there by portal at the end of the Ustei expedition. The scholars: "Scholars of the arts. Painting, poetry, sculpture, dance"; people travel from across the continent to visit its theatres. People: almost entirely human and very dark-skinned, with local fashion loose and breathable, calmer than the Ustei's. Rule: a Duke of Boko, a silver-ranker through cores, as is normal for political leaders; noble houses exist. Adventurers: the Adventure Society has a branch, but Boko "was not a strong adventuring city". Trouble: a movement against intellectuals among low-rankers began in Boko proper before it spread out; officials suspect more sinister backing and a power base shift to Greenstone and Boko. Book 1: the Adventure Society returns the Ustei captives to Boko, where Jason arrives through Hester's portal; he, Gary and Rufus explore it. After the assassination the city is evacuated, the blast containment zone gives out and the city is gone; most of its ninety thousand people are evacuated.
47.name: Boko

48.content: Belinda "Lindy" Callahan is Sophie's oldest friend, a thief from Greenstone's Old City who becomes Clive's assistant and, in time, the team's planner, infiltrator and master of shapeshifting. Essences: Magic, Trap and Adept, which she traded for in Book 2, producing the Charlatan confluence. Abilities: Echo Spirit is her first charlatan ability; Bait and Switch, Rune Trap, Force Tether, Lightning Tether and Pit of the Reaper; shapeshifting. Storage: a personal storage space that even the Magic Society cannot peek into "without killing her first". Familiars: Shimmer, a summoned astral lantern, and an echo spirit that looks like a blurry version of her.
48.name: Belinda Callahan

49.content: Clive Standish is a tall, lanky Magic Society researcher in Greenstone, raised on an eel farm, who becomes Jason's team's ritualist and astral-magic scholar. He explains the cosmos to Jason as a bowl of dumpling soup, identifies the Reaper-trial astral space as a Builder vessel, and builds the open-access Magical Research Association. A lecturer who loses the thread and apologises; he wants dumpling soup in the middle of his own lecture on the cosmos. He says he venerates, not worships, the Celestial Book: "There's a difference"; an archbishop asks "You admit to being a heretic?" and Clive answers that he "could be considered a heretic". He jokes about his background: "I'm the son of eel farmers". A stranger accuses him of sleeping with a wife he says he does not have, which becomes a running gag. Essences: Magic, Rune, Balance and the Karmic confluence. A rune essence came to him as "an epic four-star essence". Abilities: Wrath of the Magister, a rune circle that triggers effects when attacked, the damage-reflecting buff Mantle of Retribution and the zone ability Eye of Karma; Mana Equilibrium. Racial gift: a blessing from the Celestial Book changed his human Special Attack Affinity into a spell affinity. Familiar: Onslow, a rune tortoise who sits at the prow of the airboat, carries Clive, and becomes a runic tattoo on his torso when called back. Ritual and astral magic: he leads the team's rituals and bridge research.
49.name: Clive Standish

50.content: Danielle Geller is Humphrey's mother and the head of the Geller family's household in Greenstone. She is a silver-ranker at the start of the series who looks much younger than she is, later a gold-ranker with dimension and time powers, and Jason's political adviser on Earth. Time: a time confluence, with only forward time travel possible; in Book 3 she outpaces Lucian Lamprey in a fight, teleporting behind him and cutting his neck. She is called "Time Witch of Vitesse". Dimension: a dimension essence, as Emir says, with gold rank from the notes; she teleports behind Lamprey in a fight. Estate and training: the Geller estate's mirage chamber can run at bronze rank only "for limited periods" because Greenstone's magic is low, and at iron rank Danielle offers it to Rufus; a family member from the generation that first settled the region may still be alive. The diamond-rank ancestor in the earlier notes was not found.
50.name: Danielle Geller

key: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
51.comment: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
51.content: A familiar is a purely magical creature from the deep astral given a body by a summoning. Jason has three, each very different, and Humphrey has one.
keys: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash
51.name: The Familiars: Shade, Colin, Gordon and Stash

52.content: Farrah Hurin (also spelt Huren) is a small, pale, strawberry-blonde ritual magician from Vitesse. She is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, teaches him aura control, perception and meditation, and treats him as an equal. Essences: Earth, Fire and Potent, which form the Volcano confluence; she explains this herself in Book 1. Abilities: lava cannon, a magma golem, lava streams and fire orbs, obsidian domes, shards and columns, and obsidian armour. Ritual magic: she adjusts circles for ambient magic and builds the infrastructure of Asano Village and the Grid repairs. Aura teaching: perception and memory games, meditation and aura control.
52.name: Farrah Hurin

53.content: Gareth "Gary" Xandier is an enormous leonid smith and warrior from Vitesse. He makes Jason's first sword, Dread Salvation. Summon: a foundry golem, a roughly three-metre black-iron figure with a molten mouth that drips molten metal. Equipment: conjured full-body dark-steel plate armour; the notes add a hammer and shield and the runes. Smithing: he forges Dread Salvation; he reforges it with his mentor Virid Martine as Hegemon's Will. Rank: bronze at the start; "almost silver" by Book 3; silver after using a core. Demigod: Hero's power makes him a demigod, "a vision of physical might, wreathed in divine power".
53.name: Gary (Gareth Xandier) and Gary Sharpton

54.content: Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller is the leader of Team Biscuit, a tall, broad-shouldered, handsome young man from a family that has been adventuring for sixteen generations. He begins the series a shy teenager and becomes a steady leader and one of the team's strongest fighters. Formal in a crisis: in Book 3, facing the Builder's forces, he announces "My name is Humphrey Francis Eugene Geller. My family have been adventurers for sixteen generations. We aren't alchemists or weaponsmiths on the side... For hundreds of years we have done one thing, and one thing only: protect our world from people like you". Shy in personal matters: when Jason asks in front of his mother whether he has spoken to Gabrielle, he turns white and shakes his head. Moral voice: in Book 1 he confronts Jason about the cruelty of the mirage-arena ambush. He later advises against elaborate plans: "We tried that fifteen years ago and we only got from Rimaros to Yaresh". Essences: the dragon confluence, reached through the might and wing essences. Abilities include dragon wings and a flaming dragon-wing sword, a Dragon's Might aura that turns fire into dragon fire, teleporting, and the ability Spartoi, which at gold rank calls up a hundred dragon-tooth bone-golem warriors in blue and gold armour. Racial gift: his human gift Special Attack Affinity evolves into Attack of the Mirage Dragon and later into Hero's Drive, with the racial gift Hero's Sacrifice.
54.name: Humphrey Geller

55.content: Jason Asano is the series' protagonist: an Australian from the coastal town of Casselton Beach who, at twenty-three, is pulled across the cosmos to Pallimustus by a failed summoning. Humour and references: he jokes constantly and quotes films and television. He tells the Builder it and Knowledge "should get together and play Mario Kart"; he compares a projected face to Emperor Palpatine. He says "G'day" and "mate". Self-deprecation: "I'm only twenty-three but I've been pretty efficient about squandering my opportunities". He does not celebrate his birthday, which falls on 1 April: "It's not a celebratory time. I never liked my birthday anyway". Essences: Dark, Blood, Sin and the Doom confluence. His attributes are bound as Power (Blood), Speed (Dark), Spirit (Doom) and Recovery (the fourth essence). Way of the Reaper martial arts. The set Regalia of the Dark Hegemon includes the Amulet of the Dark Guardian. Abilities seen in the text: Path of Shadows, Midnight Eyes, Castigate and Verdict, Punition, Feast of Absolution and Gordon's Harbinger of Doom. Outworlder racial abilities: Interface, Quest System, Inventory, Map, Astral Affinity and Mysterious Stranger. Mysterious Stranger gives language adaptation, absorption of essences, awakening stones and skill books, and immunity to identification and tracking effects. Astral Affinity increases resistance to dimension effects and astral forces and increases the effect of dimension abilities and transcendent damage.
55.name: Jason Asano

56.content: Knowledge is the goddess of Knowledge. Jason meets her in Book 1 on arriving at her temple, and for twelve books she charms and manipulates him.
56.name: Knowledge

57.content: Neil Davone is an elf of Greenstone's Island families, a healer who grows from the Mercers' hanger-on into the heart of Jason's team. He is a priest of the Healer, and by 2038 he uses his growth magic to reclaim deserts. Essences: Shield, Growth and Renewal, producing the Prosperity confluence: short-lived shields that intercept attacks, healing and cleansing. Abilities: size-growth power and Armour of Renewal, which reduces damage taken and gives healing over time; the Reaper's Redoubt. Summon: a chrysalis golem "like an ogre carved out of diamond" with runes appearing on its facets as it is hit. Late: his Growth, Renewal and Prosperity essences find fertile ground in desert reclamation in Australia and North Africa.
57.name: Neil Davone

58.content: Rufus Remore is a bald, dark-skinned swordsman from Vitesse, grandson of the diamond-ranker Roland Remore. He is one of the three adventurers Jason meets in the Vane cellar, runs Jason's field assessment, and remains his friend for the rest of the series. He is calm under pressure: when Anisa demands that Jason be burned as tainted, he answers "I did [know]" and refuses her any say. He feels responsible as the leader of his group: Farrah tells Jason "Rufus is in charge, so he blames himself" for their capture, and says the pressure on him from his family is enormous. After Farrah's death he is driven by obsession, which strains his relationships. Swordsmanship: an elegant scimitar of golden light with red-gold inscriptions that he conjures in his hand; silver and golden swords. Other powers: boots that let him walk on water and a "speed of light" power that makes the world "seem to freeze in time" for "two seconds of accelerated time". Kingdom of Eclipse: a sun-and-moon power invoked by incantation. Teaching: he teaches Jason footwork, balance and combat and later teaches the Asano clan.
58.name: Rufus Remore

59.content: Sophie Wexler is a celestine fighter known as the Nightingale in the Greenstone fighting pits. She is a thief and debt-slave when Jason meets her, has her indenture taken over by Jason in Book 2, and becomes the team's fastest fighter and, later, Humphrey's fiancée. Essences: Swift, Balance and Wind, producing the Mystic confluence: Clive answers "Mystic" when Rufus asks what that combination produces. Before Jason's help she had only the Swift essence and its single ability for more than half a dozen years. Abilities: Eternal Moment, a massive acceleration power in which "time seemed to freeze" as she produced wind blades; Between the Raindrops; Mirage Step and Wind Blade; unarmed Way of the Reaper strikes. Racial gifts (celestine): Mana Integrity evolves into Mana Wellspring, Astral Affinity into Boundary Breaker, which removes the damage reduction from rank disparity, and Celestial Swiftness into Princess of the Firmament.
59.name: Sophie Wexler

60.content: Single-use stones that awaken an essence ability, found, traded and rewarded by rank and rarity. What they do: "An awakening stone that unlocks the power of consumption... Effect: Awakens an essence ability", requiring an unawakened essence ability. The stone melts into the user's hand "with little fanfare". Why they matter: Rufus tells Jason he cannot "properly progress towards bronze rank until you awaken every essence ability you have. That's all twenty". Naming and rarity: stones are "unranked" and carry a rarity, such as the Awakening Stone of the Feast, of Adventure, of the Stars and of the Reaper. Affinity: the Reaper stone "sharing affinity with the Reaper" is used in Jason's awakening ritual with the Reaper token, and it gives Humphrey, a human, a special attack. Divine awakening stones: a god-made stone is "transcendent rank, epic" and bestows a specific aura power. Sources: looting an awakening stone or essence can pay better than the contract to kill the monster; the Adventure Society gives stones for exceptional service, "although rarely", and some open contracts offer them as rewards; otherwise stones are bought through brokers, almost always at auction, at exorbitant prices. Brokers in a small city hold the valuable stuff, like essences and stones, for big auctions. Family supply: the Gellers traditionally supply their scions with enough stones to get started, while the rest must be earned.
60.name: Awakening Stones

61.content: Emir's cloud ship and palace, and Jason's own cloud houses, yachts and palaces made from his Cloud Flask. Emir's cloud ship: it arrives at the Greenstone dock and a walkway of cloud connects to the shore as a hole opens in its side. Moored, it morphs over about ten minutes into a palace of clouds floating on the water. Emir's cloud palace: floating just offshore on the north side of the Island, "fully exposed to the waves and currents, yet remained as immovable as solid ground", with wings and towers in blue, purple, orange and gold. Walls, floors and ceilings glow with absorbed sunlight the palace stores and distributes, and the floors have a bouncy-castle spring. Low-magic limits: out of Greenstone the ship's full functionality is restored when Emir's cloud ship floats above Kurdansk. Team base: Jason's team move into Emir's palace after the contest. Jason's Cloud Flask: it creates buildings and vehicles of cloud, with forms limited by rank, iron cloud houses, bronze cloud vehicles and silver cloud palaces; items inside a returned construct are stored in a dimensional space until another is formed. Asano Village: Farrah prepares a place for Jason's cloud house at the end of a glass tunnel along the seafloor, two kilometres out, reached by a tramway from the compound and sealed by a wall of water, so the house can run underwater; the text checked does not show the house later sitting there.
61.name: Cloud Constructs and Cloud Palaces

key: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
62.comment: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
62.content: Single-use and crafting items: the City of Fallen Echoes rewards, clockwork cores, reality cores and star seeds. Lesser Miracle Potion: "iron rank, legendary", "Salvation in a bottle", it fully restores health, mana and stamina but only works on normal and iron-rank people, and its lingering magic delays other recovery. Medallion of Escape: "silver rank, uncommon", evacuates the holder from the astral space when their aura is projected into it, and only works inside the City of Fallen Echoes. Immortal Crest: "iron rank, rare", lets a mystical tattooist draw out a soul crest and only works on an iron-rank essence user. Summoner's Die: Form: "iron rank [growth], legendary", it randomly alters the form of an iron-rank summon. Clockwork Core: "iron rank, rare", the core of an artificial monster that simplifies the materials and processes of a construct creature; clockwork cores are made by clockwork kings. Star seeds: great astral beings, not gods, "can send their followers star seeds"; once implanted and germinated the body transforms, "minor or major". Reality cores: roughly the size and shape of an ostrich egg, dark crystal glowing with transcendent light; one appears in each affected zone and the factions scramble for it.
keys: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials
62.name: Consumables, Trial Rewards and Crafting Materials

key: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
63.comment: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
63.content: The vehicles that cross the desert around Greenstone: the sand skimmers and sand barges Emir Bahadir's people run, the carriages that move expeditions to relay stations, and the monstrous Ustei war barge. Emir's cloud ship is covered in Cloud_Constructs_and_Palaces.md. Sand skimmers: small desert vehicles that carry a party across the sand. Emir leaves skimmers waiting at Boko to carry the team into the desert. Pushed past their limits: one of Emir's people specialises in magical tools and can periodically push the skimmers to speeds beyond their normal capability, so the whole vehicle vibrates. Their limits: skimmers cannot go through an astral-space aperture, so the party continues on foot. Requisitioned skimmers: expeditions requisition extra skimmers from the city and return them afterwards. Sand barges: larger vessels that move people and supplies overland. After Emir's ship sails south down the coast and into shore at an unremarkable patch of desert, his people unload three sand barges that carry the whole group inland to Sky Scar Lake. The trip takes hours more, into the night. Expedition transport: an expedition leaving Greenstone uses carriages to reach desert relay stations, then the captured Ustei barge and smaller barges supplied by the Magic Society.
keys: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges
63.name: Desert Transport: Skimmers and Sand Barges

key: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
64.comment: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
64.content: ; Dread Salvation: a sword "crafted with gratitude, in hope it would be of the greatest use in the moment of greatest need"; "iron rank [growth], legendary"; when an affliction special attack meets a physical immunity it gains Stone Cutter, and for a magical immunity Spell Breaker. Gary made it, as a gift. The window says it "must be reforged by the original craftsperson in order to advance further". Cloud Flask: iron rank growth item that Jason binds in Book 2; it creates cloud buildings and vehicles, with forms limited by rank. Its maker is "some unknown diamond-rank craftsman". Amulet of the Dark Guardian: silver rank growth item, the last item produced by his old quest system, a reproduction of his personal crest on an obsidian chain. Its boon Guardian's Blessing absorbs damage per affliction applied and can be given to another person by touch. Regalia of the Dark Hegemon: the set bonuses are Hegemon's Authority from the amulet (allies in his aura resist aura suppression, and he can spend instances to strengthen his own suppression), a mist shroud from the cloud flask, and mana drain with Hegemon's Tribute from the sword. Robes of the Astral Verdict: bronze rank, rare cloth armour for summoners that boosts dimension spells, summon damage reduction and disruptive-force resistance.
keys: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
64.name: Soul-Bound Items and the Regalia of the Dark Hegemon
